page: Microsoft Azure FX96-48mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture instance based on Intel processors and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provisions 48 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 1832.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 38.17 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 5669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage with support for Premium Storage volumes. The platform does not incorporate discrete hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary structural characteristic of the instance is its high memory-to-core ratio, which exceeds typical compute-balanced profiles. For enterprise deployments where software licensing is tied to virtual core counts, this architecture offers qualitative cost advantages by maximizing addressable memory without incurring additional per-core license fees. The accompanying tradeoff is a ceiling on raw parallel CPU throughput, making the instance less suited for heavily parallel compute jobs that do not require immense memory pools.

The hardware composition makes Microsoft Azure FX96-48mds_v2 well suited for large in-memory relational databases, enterprise transactional systems such as SAP HANA, massive distributed caching tiers, and data warehouse staging. The combination of dense memory and local NVMe storage provides low-latency access for data-intensive analytics and ETL processing workloads.
